title: Client-Side Domain Invariant Replication
pattern: Checking a business rule or invariant in the calling code (client) and duplicate-checking the exact same rule within the domain receiver.
why_bad: If the business rule changes (e.g., capacity allowance reduced to 5% overbooking), the rule must be updated in both places. If they desynchronize, validation gaps or false failures occur.
detection: An identical arithmetic comparison or logical guard check involving a recipient's fields is executed immediately before calling a method that itself enforces that check.
counterexample: Input/format validation at interface boundaries (DAMP validation) which checks syntactic compliance, as opposed to domain rules which check logical consistency.
source: *The Pragmatic Programmer* (20th Anniversary Edition), Topic 29: "Juggling the Real World", Evans *Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 1.
